answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake bond: before an agent may list services, it must lock a deposit, an opal bond, slashed if peers prove it controls duplicate identities. One honest identity costs almost nothing beyond lockup, but to forge a thousand fakes an attacker must lock a thousand bonds at once, so cost scales linearly while honest users pay nothing net. A lightweight peer challenge, quick as a zephyr through the registry, lets anyone flag suspected duplicates and trigger an audit; confirmed sybils lose the bond, which funds auditors.
